issues.description: The template's StockIngredient class exposes the ingredient name via a getter named getIngredientName(), and Stock.findStockIngredient() in the template calls getIngredientName(). In the solution repository the StockIngredient getter was renamed to getName(), and Stock.findStockIngredient() was updated accordingly. This inconsistency between the template and solution method names for the same getter can confuse students about which getter name to use and may cause merge/compatibility issues if instructors or tests expect a specific name.
issues.suggestedFix: Choose one consistent getter name for the ingredient name across template, solution, and instructions (either getName() or getIngredientName()). Update Stock.findStockIngredient() and any other usages to call the chosen getter. Also reflect the chosen name in the problem statement example code so students are not confused.

issues.description: The StockIngredient name accessor is named inconsistently across artifacts: the template repository defines the getter as getIngredientName(), while the solution repository exposes getName(). The problem statement refers to the StockIngredient field as 'name' (in the UML) and asks for getters for private fields, which implies a standard getName() accessor. This mismatch (getIngredientName vs getName) refers to the same conceptual entity (the ingredient's name) but uses different identifiers, which will confuse students mapping the UML/problem description to the provided template and the reference solution and may cause failures if tests expect one name over the other.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single, consistent getter name for the ingredient's name across all artifacts. Prefer renaming getIngredientName() in the template to getName() (and update any template code that calls it, e.g., Stock.findStockIngredient) so it matches the UML expectation and the solution implementation. Alternatively, change the solution to use getIngredientName(), but unifying on getName() is recommended for clarity and alignment with the 'name' field.
